title: Israel's dashed ambitions to topple the Iranian regime
subhead: The Israeli government thought it could take advantage of the war launched with the US on February 28 to bring down the Islamic Republic. But the Mossad intelligence agency's plans to enlist the help of Kurdish opposition groups and former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad failed.

subhead: Admired for his simplicity and humility, he was the first monarch born in Norway in nearly six centuries. He died on Friday at the age of 89.

title: Treatments and vaccines under trial amid the worst Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo's history
subhead: More than 2,700 people have died since the official declaration of the epidemic in the DRC in mid-May. Health organizations are racing to develop effective therapies, including antivirals, monoclonal antibodies and vaccines.

title: Ulaanbaatar transformed by rural exodus as the city's youth search for their place, in pictures
subhead: As the Mongolian capital hosts the UNCCD COP17, which began August 17, Le Monde is showcasing photographer Odhran Dunne's work. In 2025, he turned his lens on this rapidly changing city, capturing portraits of its youth while exploring their hopes and memories of the steppes.

title: The Suez Canal's early years, under the shadow of the French and British empires
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (3/6). From 1880 to 1914, Egypt received less than 1% of the revenue generated by the Suez Canal Company. That income illustrated the United Kingdom's and France's domination of the waterway's management at the beginning of the 20th century.

title: The Suez Canal: Birth and death of a colonial myth
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (1/6). In 1869, the creation of a maritime route linking the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, operated by the French and the British, captivated Europe. Initially a symbol of colonial oppression for the Egyptian people, the waterway became a tool of emancipation when President Nasser announced its nationalization 70 years ago, on July 26, 1956.
